newsitem.title: CHINA: China bankers uncover corrupt grain officials.
newsitem.headline: China bankers uncover corrupt grain officials.

text.p: Bank authorities in northwestern China have unmasked corrupt grain dealers who siphoned off 4.86 billion yuan ($585 million) in state loans meant to boost agriculture, Xinhua news agency said on Saturday.
More than 200 dealers in the northwestern province of Jilin had diverted the loans to buy cars, apartments and to finance other business operations, the official agency said.

The cases were uncovered by the state-run Agricultural Development Bank, which had also discovered that a number of officials in state grain departments and agricultural companies were diverting millions of yuan for their own use, it said.
Judicial officials had begun action against those involved, arresting six people and investigating others, it said.

Grain officials in the northeastern province of Heilongjiang and in central Henan province had also been arrested in cases involving thousands of tonnes of wheat and corn and major economic losses, the agency said.
Leaders at one Henan depot who built apartment buildings and bought luxury cars while neglecting grain management had been arrested for economic crimes, it said.

Officials in Heilongjiang had misused their powers and taken hundreds of thousands of yuan in bribes, it said, adding that authorities had told grain departments to improve management and to be on the lookout for illegal activities.
A large proportion of China's grain crop is still bought by the state at prices well below market levels, creating money-making opportunites for unscrupulous officials.
Financial corruption, almost unknown under the strict communist rule of former Chairman Mao Zedong, has surged in China as nearly two decades of economic reform weaken social controls.
